goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts is constructed from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar/video updates run against the wrong account and updateCalendarAttendees silently fails when an attendee or team admin adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (team admin/owner or an existing attendee). However, it constructs the EventManager with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not with the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer`) or the booking owner's stored credentials (even though the booking query includes `user.credentials`). Since `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is meant to update the calendar event for the booking (which is typically owned by the organizer/booking user), running it with the caller’s credentials will target the wrong account when the caller is not the organizer, and can cause calendar updates to fail or update the wrong calendar. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff and is a correctness defect introduced by the new handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest email check is case-sensitive: the blacklist is lower-cased on load but the incoming guest address is compared raw, so addresses like Blocked@Example.com bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and candidate issue describe the same flaw: the blacklist entries are lowercased, but the incoming guest email is not normalized before using includes(), making the check effectively case-sensitive and allowing uppercase variants to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var is split on ',' without trimming whitespace, making entries with leading/trailing spaces unmatchable

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is parsed with `split(",").map(email => email.toLowerCase())` but without `.trim()`. If the env var contains spaces around commas (e.g., "a@x.com, b@y.com"), the second entry becomes " b@y.com" and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` will not match a normal "b@y.com" guest string, so the blacklist can be bypassed unintentionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts guests array has no max length and no rate limiting, allowing any attendee to create thousands of attendee rows and outbound emails (spam amplification)

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces a new authed TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in addGuests.schema.ts) accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or other bound). The handler then:
- builds `uniqueGuests` from that array (only filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, not limiting count),
- writes all of them via `attendees.createMany`, and
- calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which generates outbound email sends for organizer/team members and then maps over all `calendarEvent.attendees` to send emails.

Because permission allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call the mutation, an attendee can submit a very large `guests` array and cause potentially thousands of DB inserts and outbound emails. The lack of a max length is directly verifiable in the diff; explicit rate limiting is also not present anywhere in the added route/handler code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner instead of ||, wrongly denying team admins with FORBIDDEN
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && instead of || when determining admin/owner access, which incorrectly requires both roles and denies admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees and does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted guests array, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees and fails to deduplicate repeated emails within the submitted guests array, which can lead to createMany inserting duplicate attendee rows. This matches the core issue in the golden comment (lack of input deduplication leading to duplicate inserts), even though it omits mention of blacklisted emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-then-write race condition: the 'already an attendee' check reads previously fetched booking.attendees before an unguarded createMany, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent calls insert duplicates

adjudication.rationale:
The handler does a classic read-then-write: it loads `booking.attendees`, filters `guests` against that snapshot (`uniqueGuests`), then performs `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without a transaction/locking or `skipDuplicates`. This means concurrent `addGuests` calls can both decide the same email is “not an attendee yet” and attempt to insert it.

However, the proposed finding’s key assertion—“there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)”—is not verifiable from this diff (the Prisma schema / DB constraints are not shown). If such a unique constraint exists, the issue would manifest as intermittent write errors rather than silent duplicate rows. Because the finding hinges on an unproven absence of a unique constraint, it’s not fully verifiable as stated from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so existing attendees receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notice

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) but calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` input. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing the raw list means any already-existing attendee emails present in the input will satisfy `includes(...)` and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the add-guests notification, whereas passing `uniqueGuests` would avoid that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) comparison in email-manager.ts is case-sensitive against the stored address

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)`, the check `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is a strict, case-sensitive string comparison. In this diff, `newGuests` comes from `addGuestsHandler` as the raw `guests` input (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`), and neither `addGuests.schema.ts` nor the handler normalizes emails (e.g., lowercasing). Attendee emails in `calendarEvent.attendees` originate from DB (`bookingAttendees.attendees`) and may differ in case from user input. This can misclassify an actually-new guest as an existing attendee (or vice versa), sending the wrong email template.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The constructed evt never sets team, so sendAddGuestsEmails skips team-member notifications and the attendee subject falls back to the organizer name instead of the team name for team event types

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes `organizer`, `attendees`, `destinationCalendar`, etc., but never sets a `team` field. However, `sendAddGuestsEmails` relies on `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` and then checks `calendarEvent.team?.members` to send `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to team members; with no `team` on `evt`, that branch will be skipped. Additionally, `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` builds the subject with `name: this.calEvent.team?.name || this.calEvent.organizer.name`, so for team bookings it will fall back to organizer name because `team` is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCalendarAttendees is awaited without try/catch after the DB write commits, so a calendar-provider failure throws an error to the user and prevents sendAddGuestsEmails from running, leaving guests added with no notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the DB update that creates new attendees is executed first via prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...). After that commits, the code does `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no try/catch. If the calendar-provider update throws (network/provider error), the handler will throw and exit before reaching the subsequent `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch { ... }` block. This produces the inconsistent state described: guests are persisted in DB but no emails are sent (and potentially no calendar update), and the error propagates back to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of booking.status or start time, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or past bookings and receive an ICS with status CONFIRMED

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts) loads a booking by `id` and, after only permission + email uniqueness/blacklist checks, unconditionally updates `booking.attendees` and triggers calendar/email notifications. There is no check against any booking lifecycle fields (e.g., cancelled/rejected status) and no check that `startTime/endTime` are in the future. Additionally, the new email templates used by `sendAddGuestsEmails` generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts) regardless of the booking state. So guests can be added and receive a CONFIRMED ICS even if the booking is cancelled/rejected or already in the past.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests accompany the new handler: permission matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/unrelated user), blacklist filtering, and duplicate filtering are all untested despite new e2e data-testid hooks

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new behavior (new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, new permission logic, blacklist/duplicate filtering, and new UI hooks like `data-testid="add_members"`/`add-emails"`) but does not add or modify any test files. This makes the claim that these cases are untested verifiable from the diff itself (no unit/integration/e2e tests accompany the new handler/UI).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, so the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner persists the next time the dialog opens

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when local Zod validation fails in `handleAdd()`. If the user then fixes the emails and successfully submits, `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` to `[""]` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail` to `false`. Since the component remains mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and the `Dialog` is controlled via the `open` prop), the stale `isInvalidEmail === true` will still be present the next time the dialog is opened, causing the error banner to appear even with a fresh input state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx error message template `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always non-empty, making the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback dead code and showing users raw text like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `message` is built with a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always returns a string (at minimum something like `"undefined: "`), so `message` will always be truthy and `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback. Also, since it concatenates `err.data?.code` (e.g., `FORBIDDEN`) and `t(err.message)` (which may fall back to the raw key if not translated), users can indeed see raw-ish output like `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: catch (err) in addGuests.handler.ts logs a fixed string and discards err, making email failures undiagnosable; should log the error object and use the project logger instead of console.log

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block logs only a fixed string and discards the caught `err`, so the actual failure details are lost, making production email-send issues hard to diagnose. It also uses `console.log` rather than any structured/project logger (if one exists), which further reduces observability. This is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx uses key={index} for a list whose middle items can be removed, causing React to reuse the wrong EmailField and jump focus/validation state to the neighboring row

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx the list renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)` and supports removing arbitrary rows via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. When an item is removed from the middle, all subsequent items shift indices, so React will reuse the existing EmailField component instances for different emails. This is a known correctness/UX issue for dynamic lists (can cause focus/cursor position and any internal input/validation state to jump to a neighboring row).

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws an opaque Prisma P2025 500 for bookings with null userId instead of a typed tRPC error, and is a redundant query since booking.user is already included

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The use of `booking.userId || 0` indicates `userId` may be null/undefined; if it is, Prisma will query `id = 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (typically a Prisma P2025) which is not converted to a typed `TRPCError` in this handler, resulting in an internal/opaque error response. Also, the initial booking query already includes `user`, so this second user lookup is avoidable by selecting the needed organizer fields in the original `include`/`select` (even though the current include doesn’t select name/email/timeZone/locale).

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmailLazy.tsx comment 'These are like 40kb that not every user needs' is copy-pasted from PhoneInputLazy and is factually false for the ~2KB MultiEmail component

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a comment in `packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx` saying "These are like 40kb that not every user needs". However, the proposed finding asserts the comment is factually false because `MultiEmail` is ~2KB, and that size claim is not verifiable from the diff (no bundle analysis or size info is provided). Also, even if the comment were inaccurate, it is a documentation/comment nit rather than a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx imports from the @calcom/ui barrel that re-exports it, creating a circular import; should import Button/EmailField/Icon/Tooltip from concrete module paths

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button/EmailField/Icon/Tooltip` from the `@calcom/ui` barrel (`import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";`). The same barrel (`packages/ui/index.tsx`) now re-exports `MultiEmail` via `export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy";`, and `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` dynamically imports `./MultiEmail`. This creates a circular dependency chain: `MultiEmail.tsx -> @calcom/ui (index.tsx) -> MultiEmailLazy.tsx -> (dynamic import) MultiEmail.tsx`. Even if the dynamic import can mitigate some runtime issues, the circular import is real and verifiable from the diff and is a reasonable review concern.
